title: Scoquams Creek / Schookwames Neck
summary: Scoquams is recorded as a neck of land and small creek in Islip, east of Babylon village.
history_content: A 1740 deed described Scoquams as the small creek east of Sampowams River. Later forms include Sequams, Scoquaumes, and Schookwames.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Scoquams, Schookwames, Skookwams, Schookwaumes, Sequam, and Scoquam. Later local interpretation described the name as snake neck or snake place, while Skookwams is treated as a corrupted form of the earlier Scoquams name.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names carry knowledge that has been passed from generation to generation - they are the story maps that once connected Indigenous people to place and guided Indigenous people from place to place.”

— Bob Joseph, The Relationship Between Indigenous Peoples and Place Names (n.d.), opening explanation
preservation_content: Scoquams links West Islip shoreline geography with Native personal naming and with the boundary language of town and deed records.
